static int rv_wait_slot(struct rv_playback_s *pb,
                        struct rv_slot_s *slot)
{
  int ret;

  if (pb == NULL || slot == NULL)
    {
      return -EINVAL;
    }

  for (;;)
    {
      int inflight;
      int result;

      ret = rv_lock(pb);
      if (ret < 0)
        {
          return ret;
        }

      inflight = slot->inflight;
      result = slot->result;
      rv_unlock(pb);

      if (!inflight)
        {
          if (result < 0 && result != -ECANCELED)
            {
              return result;
            }
          return 0;
        }

      if (pb->stopped)
        {
          return -ECANCELED;
        }

      ret = nxsem_wait_uninterruptible(&slot->done);
      if (ret < 0)
        {
          return ret;
        }
    }
}

static int rv_queue_slot(struct rv_playback_s *pb,
                         struct rv_slot_s *slot,
                         const uint8_t *src, size_t len,
                         bool final_block)
{
  struct audio_buf_desc_s desc;
  struct ap_buffer_s *apb;
  uint8_t *dst;
  size_t frames;
  size_t tx_len;
  size_t i;
  int ret;

  if (pb == NULL || slot == NULL || src == NULL || len == 0 ||
      len > RV_SOURCE_BLOCK_BYTES)
    {
      return -EINVAL;
    }

  len &= ~(size_t)1;
  if (len == 0)
    {
      return -EINVAL;
    }

  frames = len / sizeof(int16_t);
  tx_len = frames * RV_WIRE_BYTES_PER_SAMPLE;
  if (tx_len == 0 || tx_len > RV_WIRE_BLOCK_BYTES)
    {
      return -EINVAL;
    }

  /*
   * Normal blocks keep the proven 2048-byte wire contract.
   *
   * F7P exception: Media may submit one terminal short tail.  Its APB nbytes
   * is the exact converted wire length (for example 512 source bytes become
   * 1024 wire bytes).  contest_i2s shortens that descriptor and terminates
   * the cyclic ring after the real final samples.
   */
  if (RV_WIRE_BLOCK_BYTES != RV_LOWER_DMA_SLOT_BYTES)
    {
      return -EINVAL;
    }

  ret = rv_wait_slot(pb, slot);
  if (ret < 0)
    {
      return ret;
    }

  if (pb->stopped) return -ECANCELED;

  /* One stable APB per upper playback slot.  The lower half copies every
   * submitted block into its private immutable DMA ring payload. */
  if (slot->apb == NULL)
    {
      memset(&desc, 0, sizeof(desc));
      desc.numbytes = RV_WIRE_BLOCK_BYTES;
      desc.u.pbuffer = &slot->apb;

      ret = apb_alloc(&desc);
      if (ret < 0 || slot->apb == NULL)
        {
          slot->apb = NULL;
          return ret < 0 ? ret : -ENOMEM;
        }

      RV_VERBOSE("[RV-PB] fixed APB slot=%u ptr=%p bytes=%u\n",
             slot->index, slot->apb->samp, RV_WIRE_BLOCK_BYTES);
    }

  apb = slot->apb;

  /*
   * Legacy/TTS short blocks still use zero padding.  Media terminal tails
   * do not pad beyond tx_len: the lower-half descriptor itself is shortened.
   */
  if (tx_len < RV_WIRE_BLOCK_BYTES &&
      !(pb->stop_on_short_underrun && (!pb->voice_live || final_block)))
    {
      memset(apb->samp, 0, RV_WIRE_BLOCK_BYTES);
    }

  dst = apb->samp;
  for (i = 0; i < frames; i++)

                ROBOT_VOICE_TTS_WORKERS;
  if (kind && !strcmp(kind, "TTS") && desired > ceiling)
    desired = ceiling;

  return desired;

static void tune_receive_buffer(int fd, int desired)
{
  int actual = 0;
  socklen_t length = sizeof(actual);
  if (desired <= 0) return;
  int read_rc = getsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_RCVBUF, &actual, &length);
  int rc = 0, error = 0;
  /* OpenVela/NuttX may implement SO_RCVBUF. Probe it instead of compiling
   * tuning out for every NuttX target. If unsupported, leave the connection
   * usable and report the failed option; do not claim the window changed.
   * Set also when a pooled socket previously served a different request kind.
   */
  if (read_rc < 0 || actual != desired) {
    rc = setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_RCVBUF, &desired, sizeof(desired));
    error = rc < 0 ? errno : 0;
    length = sizeof(actual);
    read_rc = getsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_RCVBUF, &actual, &length);
  }
  RV_EVENT("[RV-NET-TUNE] rcvbuf_requested=%d actual=%d set_rc=%d errno=%d read_rc=%d\n",
         desired, read_rc == 0 ? actual : -1, rc, error, read_rc);
}

static int tcp_connect(const char *host, const char *port,
                       unsigned long long deadline, struct rv_tls *t,
                       int receive_bytes)
{
  struct addrinfo hints, *addresses = NULL, *a;
  int fd = -1, ret = -EHOSTUNREACH;
  unsigned long long start = now_ms();
  memset(&hints, 0, sizeof(hints));
  hints.ai_family = AF_UNSPEC;
  hints.ai_socktype = SOCK_STREAM;
  /* POSIX getaddrinfo itself has no deadline API. Its platform resolver
   * timeout remains in force; all following I/O is deadline bounded. */
  t->stage = "dns";
  t->raw_error = getaddrinfo(host, port, &hints, &addresses);
  if (t->raw_error != 0) return -EHOSTUNREACH;
  RV_VERBOSE("[RV-HTTP] DNS host=%s ms=%llu\n", host, now_ms() - start);
  for (a = addresses; a; a = a->ai_next) {
    int flags;
    int poll_events = 0, so_error = -1;
    unsigned long long connect_start = now_ms();
    char peer[INET6_ADDRSTRLEN] = "unknown";
    const void *ip = NULL;
    if (a->ai_family == AF_INET)
      ip = &((struct sockaddr_in *)a->ai_addr)->sin_addr;
    else if (a->ai_family == AF_INET6)
      ip = &((struct sockaddr_in6 *)a->ai_addr)->sin6_addr;
    if (ip) (void)inet_ntop(a->ai_family, ip, peer, sizeof(peer));
    unsigned int wait_ms = remaining_ms(deadline, ROBOT_VOICE_HTTP_CONNECT_MS);
    if (!wait_ms) { ret = -ETIMEDOUT; break; }
    t->stage = "tcp-socket";
    fd = socket(a->ai_family, a->ai_socktype, a->ai_protocol);
    if (fd < 0) { ret = -errno; continue; }
    tune_receive_buffer(fd, receive_bytes);
    t->stage = "tcp-connect";
    flags = fcntl(fd, F_GETFL, 0);
    if (flags < 0 || fcntl(fd, F_SETFL, flags | O_NONBLOCK) < 0) {
      ret = -errno;
    } else if (connect(fd, a->ai_addr, a->ai_addrlen) == 0) {
      ret = 0;
    } else if (errno == EINPROGRESS || errno == EAGAIN) {
      struct pollfd pfd = {.fd = fd, .events = POLLOUT};
      int ready;
      t->stage = "tcp-poll";
      do {
        wait_ms = remaining_ms(deadline, ROBOT_VOICE_HTTP_CONNECT_MS);
        ready = wait_ms ? poll(&pfd, 1, (int)wait_ms) : 0;
      } while (ready < 0 && errno == EINTR);
      if (ready > 0) {
        int error = 0;
        socklen_t size = sizeof(error);
        poll_events = pfd.revents;
        t->stage = "tcp-so-error";
        int so_rc = getsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_ERROR, &error, &size);
        ret = so_rc == 0 ? -error : -errno;
        so_error = so_rc == 0 ? error : -1;
        if (pfd.revents & POLLNVAL) ret = -EBADF;
        else if (ret == 0 && !(pfd.revents & POLLOUT)) {
          /* Some NuttX builds report POLLERR with SO_ERROR=0 even when the
           * peer is established. Confirm the socket before treating that
           * event as a failed connect and replacing a usable descriptor. */
          struct sockaddr_storage peer_addr;
          socklen_t peer_size = sizeof(peer_addr);
          if (getpeername(fd, (struct sockaddr *)&peer_addr, &peer_size) == 0) {
            t->stage = "tcp-peer-confirmed";
          } else {
            t->stage = "tcp-poll-not-writable";
            ret = -ECONNABORTED;
          }
        }
      } else ret = ready == 0 ? -ETIMEDOUT : -errno;
#ifdef __NuttX__
      /* Retry a local poll/SO_ERROR compatibility failure on a fresh socket,
       * before sending HTTP. NuttX connect uses SO_SNDTIMEO. */
      if (ret == -EIO || ret == -ENOSYS || ret == -ENOTSUP || ret == -ENOPROTOOPT ||
          (ret == -ECONNABORTED && so_error == 0)) {
        RV_EVENT("[RV-HTTP] connect_fallback stage=%s rc=%d so_error=%d poll=0x%x\n",
                 t->stage, ret, so_error, (unsigned int)poll_events);
        close(fd);
        fd = socket(a->ai_family, a->ai_socktype, a->ai_protocol);
        t->stage = "tcp-blocking-fallback";
        if (fd < 0) ret = -errno;
        else {
          tune_receive_buffer(fd, receive_bytes);
          ret = timeout_socket(fd, remaining_ms(deadline, ROBOT_VOICE_HTTP_CONNECT_MS));
          if (ret == 0) ret = connect(fd, a->ai_addr, a->ai_addrlen) == 0 ? 0 : -errno;
          flags = 0;
        }
      }
#endif
    } else ret = -errno;
    if (ret == 0 && fcntl(fd, F_SETFL, flags & ~O_NONBLOCK) == 0) break;
    if (ret == 0) ret = -errno;
    t->raw_error = ret; t->sys_error = ret < 0 ? -ret : 0;
    RV_EVENT("[RV-TCP-ERROR] host=%s port=%s peer=%s family=%d fd=%d "
             "stage=%s rc=%d so_error=%d poll=0x%x elapsed_ms=%llu\n",
             host, port, peer, a->ai_family, fd, t->stage, ret,
             so_error, (unsigned int)poll_events, now_ms() - connect_start);
    if (fd >= 0) close(fd);
    fd = -1;
  }
  freeaddrinfo(addresses);
  if (fd >= 0) {
    int enabled = 1;
    /* Optional; unsupported socket tuning does not fail a request. */
    (void)setsockopt(fd, IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_NODELAY, &enabled, sizeof(enabled));
  }
  return fd >= 0 ? fd : ret;
}

对你当前的 **ESP32-S3 contest 工程没有实际优化效果**。

原因是：

- `ESP32_WIFI_WLAN_BUFFER_OPTIMIZATION` 只定义在经典 ESP32 的 Kconfig：[esp32/Kconfig:2217](/home/foam/vela/openvela/nuttx/arch/xtensa/src/esp32/Kconfig:2217)
- 它只被 `esp32_wlan.c` 使用，通过动态 `kmm_malloc()` 分配 WLAN 包缓冲区，减少静态 DRAM 占用。
- 当前工程使用的是 ESP32-S3 驱动：[esp32s3_wlan.c](/home/foam/vela/openvela/nuttx/arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/esp32s3_wlan.c)，该驱动没有这个配置分支。
- ESP32-S3 实际生效的是 `CONFIG_ESP32S3_WLAN_PKTBUF_NUM=24`：[.config:404](/home/foam/vela/openvela/nuttx/.config:404)

因此，给当前工程添加：

```text
CONFIG_ESP32_WIFI_WLAN_BUFFER_OPTIMIZATION=y
```

不会改变 ESP32-S3 WLAN 缓冲区实现，也不能解决当前 DRAM 溢出问题。当前使用 `CONFIG_ESP32S3_WLAN_PKTBUF_NUM=24` 才是有效的内存调整；设置为 32 已验证会导致链接阶段 DRAM 溢出。

背景数据：
- ESP32-S3 板卡运行 OpenVela/NuttX。
- CONFIG_ESP32S3_WLAN_PKTBUF_NUM=24 时，局域网 iperf：板卡接收约 0.55 Mbit/s，发送约 1.03 Mbit/s。

- 24 和 32 时都出现过：
  [WLAN-RX] NOBUF ... len=54 free=0 reserve=12 -- dropping frame
- 板卡启动日志也有 I2S DMA allocation failed，因此不能盲目增加内部静态内存。
- defconfig 中 IOB 配置为 64 个、每个 512 字节；TTS socket 实际 SO_RCVBUF 曾记录为 8192 字节。
- `ESP32_WIFI_WLAN_BUFFER_OPTIMIZATION` 在上游 Kconfig 中依赖 ARCH_CHIP_ESP32；不要假设它可用于 ESP32-S3，也不要只改 Kconfig 依赖而不实现对应源码功能。

工作要求：
1. 先检查本工程实际使用的 ESP32-S3 WLAN 驱动和构建配置，确认 CONFIG_ESP32S3_WLAN_PKTBUF_NUM 如何影响 g_wlan_priv 的内存布局，以及 `free=0`、`reserve=12` 的具体含义。不要根据上游同名配置猜测本工程实现。
2. 完整追踪 WLAN 包缓冲的申请、接收、入队、交给 NuttX 网络栈、发送和释放路径。找出 NOBUF 的直接原因，重点检查缓冲是否未及时归还、RX/TX 是否竞争同一池、队列或锁是否导致积压，以及日志计数是否可能包含重复帧。
3. 优先提出不增加 WLAN 包数的优化，例如减少重复拷贝、缩短缓冲持有时间、改善 RX/TX 池隔离或复用。只有源码和硬件约束确认允许时，才考虑把非 DMA 的大块 payload 放入 PSRAM；DMA 描述符及有 DMA 限制的内存不得擅自迁移。
4. 如果确实新增配置项，使用明确的 ESP32-S3 依赖和默认关闭状态；确保关闭时行为与当前版本一致。不要启用只适用于经典 ESP32 的配置。
5. 检查 NuttX IOB 与 WLAN 私有池的边界，避免修复 WLAN 后耗尽共享 IOB、TCP 缓冲或音频 DMA 内存。
6. 保留必要错误日志，但不要逐帧刷屏。可累计 NOBUF，并在适当时机输出统计。
7. 先给出代码路径、内存计算、根因证据和拟修改方案，再实施最小改动。不要顺手调整 TCP 窗口、任务优先级、Wi-Fi 省电、编译优化等其他变量。
8. 完成后检查代码差异，运行工程现有的相关构建或静态检查；不要声称已在实机验证。若无法交叉编译，明确说明缺少的工具或构建条件。

交付内容：
- 修改文件及路径；
- 根因和实现说明；

# NuttX Driver Development

Follow the full driver lifecycle in order. Keep edits small and testable.

> [!TIP] This skill can be used standalone or via the `driver-workflow` agent (`agents/driver-workflow.agent.md`) for end-to-end driver development with automated reference matching, requirements generation, and PR submission.

## Table of Contents

1. [Preparation](#preparation)
   - Clarify scope and expectations
   - Find reference drivers
   - Determine driver pattern
   - Layout driver files
2. [Implementation](#implementation)
   - Write driver C implementation
   - Write public header file
   - Kconfig and build system integration
   - Board-level registration
3. [NuttX Coding & Kernel API Rules](#nuttx-coding--kernel-api-rules)
4. [Code Review](#code-review)
5. [References](#references)

---

## Preparation

### 1) Clarify scope and expectations

- Identify the NuttX driver subsystem (sensor, serial, timer, analog, etc.).
- Confirm target bus (I2C, SPI, 1-Wire, etc.) and required hardware properties.
- Clarify the NuttX source tree location. The driver code lives under `nuttx/drivers/`.

### 2) Find reference drivers

> [!NOTE] Two types of reference drivers serve different purposes
>
> - **骨架参考（NuttX API 模式）**: 优先使用 NuttX in-tree 同类驱动作为代码骨架，确保符合 NuttX 的 upper-half/lower-half 架构和 VFS 集成方式
> - **芯片参考（寄存器/时序验证）**: 优先使用 Linux/Zephyr 同芯片驱动，用于交叉验证 datasheet 的寄存器定义、初始化序列、SPI 帧格式等芯片专属知识
>
> When used standalone: 手动搜索两类参考驱动
> When used with `driver-workflow` agent: Step A.2 自动完成两条线的并行搜索

Always look at the in-tree NuttX drivers before doing any work. There might already be a driver that (best scenario at the top):

1. Is exactly the same part as the one you are working on
2. Targets a very similar part from the same vendor (e.g., BMP280 vs BME680)
3. Is the same device subsystem as yours (e.g., another I2C sensor)

If a reference driver is found, use it as a **skeleton template**:

1. Copy the source file structure (function signatures, bus access pattern, registration flow, file layout)
2. Replace all device-specific content: register definitions, chip ID values, vendor/chip names, init sequences, calibration logic
3. After generating code, grep for the original chip name — zero matches required
4. **Do NOT copy register addresses or chip-specific constants** — these must come from the target device's datasheet

Re-use these files/folders whenever possible:
- Header files in `include/nuttx/sensors/`, `include/nuttx/i2c/`, etc.
- Existing board-level registration patterns in `boards/`

If no suitable reference driver exists:

1. Use the dispatch table below to load the subsystem-specific pattern reference
2. Use the most similar subsystem's reference driver as template (e.g., use accelerometer driver as template for gyro)
3. Follow the architectural pattern (uORB vs chardev) strictly from the loaded reference
4. For 🔲 Planned subsystems, use `chardev_pattern.md` (Production-Quality Skeleton section) as the starting point

Here are the relevant folders to search for examples:

```
nuttx/
├── drivers/          # Device-specific driver sources. Search here first
│   ├── sensors/      # Sensor drivers (I2C/SPI/1-Wire)
│   ├── serial/       # UART/serial drivers
│   ├── i2c/          # I2C bus framework
│   ├── spi/          # SPI bus framework
│   ├── timers/       # Timer/watchdog/RTC drivers
│   ├── analog/       # ADC/DAC drivers
│   ├── leds/         # LED drivers
│   ├── input/        # Input device drivers
│   └── ...           # Many more subsystems
├── include/nuttx/    # Public header files for driver APIs
│   ├── sensors/      # Sensor driver headers & sensor_lowerhalf_s
│   ├── i2c/          # I2C master interface (i2c_master_s)
│   ├── spi/          # SPI interface (spi_dev_s)
│   └── fs/           # VFS file_operations, register_driver()
├── boards/           # Board-specific initialization & driver registration
└── arch/             # Architecture-specific lower-half bus implementations
```

Use `references/nuttx_nav_search.md` for driver examples and navigating the NuttX repo.

### 3) Determine Driver Pattern

NuttX uses a **POSIX VFS-based** driver model. Every device appears as a file under `/dev/`. Choose the appropriate pattern based on driver subsystem type:

#### Driver Type Dispatch Table

Based on the identified subsystem, load the corresponding reference document for subsystem-specific implementation details:

| Subsystem | Pattern | Reference Document | Status |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|--------|
| **sensors** (accel, gyro, baro, temp, humi, light, mag, prox, IMU...) | Upper-Half / Lower-Half (uORB) | `references/sensor_uorb_pattern.md` | ✅ Available |
| **gnss** (GPS, GNSS, satellite positioning) | Upper-Half / Lower-Half (gnss_uorb) | `references/gnss_uorb_pattern.md` | ✅ Available |
| **net** (Ethernet, SPI-Ethernet) | Upper-Half / Lower-Half (netdev) | `references/eth_netdev_pattern.md` | ✅ Available |
| **can** (CAN, CAN FD, SocketCAN) | Upper-Half / Lower-Half (netdev) | `references/can_netdev_pattern.md` | ✅ Available |
| **lin** (LIN, LIN bus, LIN master/slave) | Upper-Half / Lower-Half (netdev, over SocketCAN) | `references/lin_netdev_pattern.md` | ✅ Available |
| **fb** (framebuffer, LCDC, display controller, 显示输出通道) | Upper-Half / Lower-Half (fb_vtable_s) | `references/fb_pattern.md` | ✅ Available |
| **lcd** (SPI/I2C LCD panel, ST7789, SSD1306, ILI9341...) | Upper-Half / Lower-Half (lcd_dev_s) | `references/lcd_pattern.md` | ✅ Available |

| **timers** (timer, watchdog, RTC) | Upper-Half / Lower-Half | `references/wdg_pattern.md` (watchdog); 待创建: `timer_pattern.md` (timer/RTC) | ✅ Partial |
| **leds** (GPIO LED, PWM LED, WS2812) | Upper-Half / Lower-Half | 待创建: `led_pattern.md` | 🔲 Planned |
| **input** (touchscreen, buttons, keyboard, mouse) | Upper-Half / Lower-Half | `references/input_pattern.md` | ✅ Available |
| **analog** (ADC, DAC) | Upper-Half / Lower-Half | 待创建: `analog_pattern.md` | 🔲 Planned |
| **serial** (UART) | Upper-Half / Lower-Half | 待创建: `serial_pattern.md` | 🔲 Planned |
| **power/battery** (charger, monitor, gauge) | Upper-Half / Lower-Half | `references/battery_charger_pattern.md` (入口) + `references/battery_ops_reference.md` (必须同时加载) | ✅ Available |
| **vibrator** | Character Device | 待创建: `vibrator_pattern.md` | 🔲 Planned |
| **usbhost-hcd** (EHCI, xHCI, DWC2, DWC3, OHCI...) | USB Host Controller Driver | `references/usbhost_hcd_pattern.md` | ✅ Available |
| **mcal** (AUTOSAR MCAL → NuttX: Uart, Spi, I2c, Adc, Can, Dma, Gpt, Icu, Pwm, Port, Wdg, Lin, Eth) | MCAL Adaptation Layer | `references/mcal_autosar_pattern.md` | ✅ Available |
| **Other / Unknown** | Standalone Character Device | `references/chardev_pattern.md` | ✅ Built-in |

> [!IMPORTANT] How to use this dispatch table
>
> 1. Identify the driver subsystem from the user's request
> 2. If the subsystem has an **✅ Available** reference → load that reference document for subsystem-specific architecture, data structures, callbacks, and registration API
>    - **Special case: USB subsystem** → The USB DCD driver is located in `nuttx/arch/<arch>/src/<chip>/`, not in `nuttx/drivers/`. The documentation loading rules are as follows:
>      - **Must be loaded** `references/usbdev_dcd_pattern.md` — The core reference for all USB DCD adapters (usbdev interface, EP0 state machine, DMA alignment, debug methods)
>      - **Must be loaded (vendor HAL adaptation)** `references/usb_bes_v2_lessons.md` — When adapting a USB DCD driver on top of a vendor HAL layer (not writing bare-metal register code), load this document for common pitfalls: HAL re-init after bus reset, speed detection, VBUS call chain tracing, callback context design, and incremental build traps. These lessons apply to all vendor HAL-based USB DCD work, not only BES.
>      - **Load on demand** `references/usb_source_lookup.md` — Load when you need to find the reference driver source code or when you are unsure of the controller IP type (Phase 1 research phase).
>      - **Load on demand** `references/usb_dwc3_case_study.md` — Load when the target controller is DWC3 or CDNS3 (TRB architecture); other IPs can be skipped, but it is recommended to browse the Bug Pattern Summary table to understand common bug patterns.
>    - **Special case: MCAL subsystem** → The MCAL adaptation layer bridges AUTOSAR MCAL modules to NuttX upper-half drivers. It is located in `frameworks/system/autocore/mcal/`, not in `nuttx/drivers/`. The documentation loading rules are as follows:
>      - **Must be loaded** `references/mcal_autosar_pattern.md` — The core reference for all MCAL adaptations (9-step workflow, architecture, code generation rules, EB Tresos config, build verification)
>      - **Must be loaded** `references/mcal_code_pattern.md` — C code templates for adaptation files (struct layout, ops callbacks, init function, ISR routing, notification callbacks, Det/Dem error reporting)
>      - **Must be loaded** `references/mcal_module_mapping.md` — MCAL→NuttX framework mapping table, cross-module dependency list with EB config steps, NuttX ops structures, MCAL API patterns, search paths
> 3. If the subsystem is **🔲 Planned** → fall back to Pattern B (standalone character device) below, and search in-tree drivers under `nuttx/drivers/<subsystem>/` for reference implementations
> 4. The reference document contains ALL subsystem-specific knowledge (data structures, callback details, registration API, data delivery modes, etc.). The main SKILL.md only contains cross-subsystem generic knowledge.

> [!NOTE] Adding a new driver subsystem reference
>
> To add support for a new driver subsystem (e.g., timers, leds, input):
> 1. Create `references/<subsystem>_pattern.md` following the structure of `sensor_uorb_pattern.md`
> 2. Include: architecture overview, key data structures, callback table, data delivery modes, registration API, complete examples
> 3. Update the Driver Type Dispatch Table above to change status from 🔲 to ✅
> 4. Add example driver paths to `references/nuttx_nav_search.md` under the corresponding subsystem section
> 5. The main SKILL.md does NOT need other modifications — the dispatch mechanism handles routing automatically

#### Pattern A: Upper-Half / Lower-Half — Preferred for Subsystem Drivers

Most NuttX driver subsystems (sensors, timers, serial, audio, etc.) use an upper-half/lower-half split. The upper-half provides the VFS interface and common logic; you only implement the lower-half callbacks.

```
Application
    │  open/read/write/ioctl/poll
    ▼
  VFS (/dev/...)
    │
    ▼
  Upper-half (provided by NuttX)  ← Generic, handles VFS + common logic
    │  subsystem-specific callbacks
    ▼
  Lower-half (your driver)  ← You implement these
    │
    ▼
  Bus API (I2C_TRANSFER / SPI_*)
```

**When to use**: Always prefer this when the subsystem provides an upper-half framework. Load the corresponding reference document from the dispatch table for implementation details.

#### Pattern B: Standalone Character Device Driver

The simplest pattern. The driver directly implements `struct file_operations` and registers with `register_driver()`.

```
Application
    │  open/read/write/ioctl/close
    ▼
  VFS (/dev/mydevN)
    │
    ▼
  file_operations  ← Your driver implements these
    │
    ▼
  Bus API (I2C_TRANSFER / SPI_LOCK+SPI_SELECT+SPI_RECVBLOCK)
```

**When to use**: Only when the device doesn't fit any existing subsystem, or when existing in-tree drivers for the same device class already use this pattern (e.g., some vibrator or custom peripheral drivers).

See `references/chardev_pattern.md` for standalone character device implementation details.

### 4) Layout the driver files

Define the files that will be created/modified. The exact layout depends on the subsystem — refer to the loaded reference document for subsystem-specific examples.

General layout:

```
nuttx/
├── drivers/<subsystem>/
│   ├── mydevice.c            # Driver implementation
│   ├── Make.defs             # Add CSRCS += mydevice.c
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Add list(APPEND SRCS mydevice.c)
│   └── Kconfig               # Add CONFIG_<SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE entry
├── include/nuttx/<subsystem>/
│   └── mydevice.h            # Public header: register function prototype
└── boards/<arch>/<chip>/<board>/src/
    └── <board>_mydevice.c    # Board-level init: get bus, call register
```

## Implementation

> [!info] TLDR
>
> - Implement C driver (lower-half callbacks OR file_operations)
> - Create public header file with register function prototype
> - Add Kconfig entry for driver enable/disable
> - Add source to Make.defs and CMakeLists.txt
> - Write board-level registration code

### Write the Driver C Implementation

For subsystem-specific implementation (sensor uORB, timer, LED, etc.), load the corresponding reference document from the Driver Type Dispatch Table above.

The following sections cover **cross-subsystem generic patterns** that apply to all driver types.

#### Bus Access (I2C / SPI)

For I2C/SPI register read/write helpers, bulk transfer patterns, SPI frame protocols (8-bit and 16-bit), and SPI mode detection — read `references/bus_access.md` when writing bus access code.

### Write the Public Header File

Create `include/nuttx/<subsystem>/mydevice.h`. The header content depends on the driver pattern:

- **Upper-half/lower-half drivers**: Header contains only the register function prototype
- **Standalone char device drivers**: Header also defines data structures for `read()`

See `references/chardev_pattern.md` for char device header examples.

### Kconfig

Add your driver entry to the appropriate `Kconfig` file (e.g., `drivers/<subsystem>/Kconfig`):

```kconfig
config <SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE
	bool "MyVendor MYDEVICE sensor/device support"
	default n
	---help---
		Enable driver for the MyVendor MYDEVICE.

if <SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE

choice
	prompt "MYDEVICE Interface"
	default <SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE_SPI

config <SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE_I2C

    86	/*
    87	 * RX reserve for the shared WLAN packet-buffer pool.
    88	 *
    89	 * RX and TX currently share pktbuf[].  During a large TCP write, devif_poll()

    92	 * pool and make wlan_rx_done() fail with -ENOBUFS, dropping TCP ACKs and
    93	 * eventually resetting the TLS connection.
    94	 *
    95	 * Keep half of the pool unavailable to normal TX polling.  RX still uses the
    96	 * full pool, so receive bursts can consume the reserve when needed.

   102	 * Upper-layer Wi-Fi TX flow control.

   126	 * The contest configuration currently uses CONFIG_NET_ETH_PKTSIZE=590.
   127	 * Log only TCP/443 traffic, with a strict rate limit, so we can determine:
   128	 *   - the MSS advertised in SYN/SYN-ACK;
   129	 *   - whether MiMo's first TLS response reaches the Wi-Fi callback;
   130	 *   - whether an incoming Ethernet frame exceeds WLAN_BUF_SIZE;
   131	 *   - whether the small wlan_pktbuf pool is exhausted.
   132	 *
   133	 * This code does not modify packets.
   134	 */
   135	#define WLAN_TLS_DIAG_PORT          443
   136	#define WLAN_TLS_DIAG_PAYLOAD_LIMIT 32 /* retained for source compatibility */
   137	
   138	static uint32_t g_wlan_tls_diag_frames;

   143	
   144	static uint16_t wlan_diag_be16(const uint8_t *p)
   145	{
   146	  return ((uint16_t)p[0] << 8) | p[1];
   147	}
   148	
   149	
   150	static uint32_t wlan_diag_be32(const uint8_t *p)
   151	{
   152	  return ((uint32_t)p[0] << 24) |
   153	         ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) |
   154	         ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8) |
   155	         (uint32_t)p[3];
   156	}
   157	
   158	
   159	static uint32_t wlan_diag_csum_add(uint32_t sum,
   160	                                   const uint8_t *data, size_t len)
   161	{
   162	  while (len >= 2)
   163	    {
   164	      sum += ((uint16_t)data[0] << 8) | data[1];
   165	      data += 2;
   166	      len -= 2;
   167	    }
   168	
   169	  if (len != 0)
   170	    {
   171	      sum += (uint16_t)data[0] << 8;
   172	    }
   173	
   174	  return sum;
   175	}
   176	
   177	static uint16_t wlan_diag_csum_fold(uint32_t sum)
   178	{
   179	  while ((sum >> 16) != 0)
   180	    {
   181	      sum = (sum & 0xffff) + (sum >> 16);
   182	    }
   183	
   184	  return (uint16_t)sum;
   185	}
   186	
   187	static bool wlan_diag_ipv4_checksum_ok(const uint8_t *ip, size_t ihl)
   188	{
   189	  uint32_t sum;
   190	
   191	  if (!ip || ihl < 20)
   192	    {
   193	      return false;
   194	    }
   195	
   196	  sum = wlan_diag_csum_add(0, ip, ihl);
   197	  return wlan_diag_csum_fold(sum) == 0xffff;
   198	}
   199	
   200	static bool wlan_diag_tcp_checksum_ok(const uint8_t *ip,
   201	                                      size_t ihl,
   202	                                      const uint8_t *tcp,
   203	                                      size_t tcp_len)
   204	{
   205	  uint32_t sum = 0;
   206	
   207	  if (!ip || !tcp || ihl < 20 || tcp_len < 20)
   208	    {
   209	      return false;
   210	    }
   211	
   212	  /* IPv4 pseudo-header: source, destination, zero, protocol, TCP length. */
   213	
   214	  sum = wlan_diag_csum_add(sum, ip + 12, 8);
   215	  sum += ip[9];
   216	  sum += (uint16_t)tcp_len;
   217	  sum = wlan_diag_csum_add(sum, tcp, tcp_len);
   218	
   219	  return wlan_diag_csum_fold(sum) == 0xffff;
   220	}

   631	/****************************************************************************
   632	 * Function: wlan_init_buffer
   633	 *
   634	 * Description:
   635	 *   Initialize the free buffer list
   636	 *
   637	 * Input Parameters:
   638	 *   priv - Reference to the driver state structure
   639	 *
   640	 * Returned Value:
   641	 *   None
   642	 *
   643	 ****************************************************************************/
   644	
   645	static inline void wlan_init_buffer(struct wlan_priv_s *priv)
   646	{
   647	  irqstate_t flags;
   648	
   649	  int i;
   650	  flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&priv->lock);
   651	
   652	  priv->dev.d_buf = NULL;
   653	  priv->dev.d_len = 0;
   654	
   655	  sq_init(&priv->freeb);
   656	  sq_init(&priv->rxb);
   657	  sq_init(&priv->txb);
   658	  priv->free_count = 0;
   659	  priv->tx_inflight = 0;
   660	  priv->tx_retry_ms = WLAN_TX_RETRY_MIN_MS;
   661	  priv->tx_retry_pending = false;
   662	  priv->tx_retry_count = 0;
   663	
   664	  for (i = 0; i < WLAN_PKTBUF_NUM; i++)
   665	    {
   666	      sq_addlast(&priv->pktbuf[i].entry, &priv->freeb);
   667	      priv->free_count++;
   668	    }
   669	
   670	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
   671	         "[WLAN-BUF] init total=%u rx_reserve=%u free=%u "
   672	         "tx_inflight_max=%u retry_ms=%u..%u retry_max=%u\n",
   673	         (unsigned int)WLAN_PKTBUF_NUM,
   674	         (unsigned int)WLAN_RX_RESERVED_BUFS,
   675	         (unsigned int)priv->free_count,
   676	         (unsigned int)WLAN_WIFI_TX_INFLIGHT_MAX,
   677	         (unsigned int)WLAN_TX_RETRY_MIN_MS,
   678	         (unsigned int)WLAN_TX_RETRY_MAX_MS,
   679	         (unsigned int)WLAN_TX_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS);
   680	
   681	  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&priv->lock, flags);

   685	 * Function: wlan_alloc_buffer

   687	 * Description:
   688	 *   Allocate one buffer from the free buffer queue

   690	 * Input Parameters:

   698	static inline struct wlan_pktbuf *wlan_alloc_buffer(struct wlan_priv_s *priv)
   699	{

   702	  sq_entry_t *entry;

   713	  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&priv->lock, flags);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: work_queue_pri
 *
 * Description: Get priority of the wqueue. We believe that all worker
 *   threads have the same priority.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *  wqueue - The work queue handle
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   SCHED_PRIORITY_MIN ~ SCHED_PRIORITY_MAX  on success,
 *   a negated errno value on failure.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int work_queue_priority(int qid);
int work_queue_priority_wq(FAR struct kwork_wqueue_s *wqueue);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: work_cancel/work_cancel_wq
 *
 * Description:
 *   Cancel previously queued work.  This removes work from the work queue.
 *   After work has been cancelled, it may be requeued by calling
 *   work_queue() again.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   qid    - The work queue ID (must be HPWORK or LPWORK)
 *   wqueue - The work queue handle
 *   work   - The previously queued work structure to cancel
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   Zero on success, a negated errno on failure
 *
 *   -ENOENT - There is no such work queued.
 *   -EINVAL - An invalid work queue was specified
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int work_cancel(int qid, FAR struct work_s *work);
int work_cancel_wq(FAR struct kwork_wqueue_s *wqueue,
                   FAR struct work_s *work);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: work_cancel_sync/work_cancel_sync_wq
 *
 * Description:
 *   Blocked cancel previously queued user-mode work.  This removes work
 *   from the user mode work queue.  After work has been cancelled, it may
 *   be requeued by calling work_queue() again.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   qid    - The work queue ID (must be HPWORK or LPWORK)
 *   wqueue - The work queue handle
 *   work   - The previously queued work structure to cancel
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   Zero means the work was successfully cancelled.
 *   One means the work was not cancelled because it is currently being
 *   processed by work thread, but wait for it to finish.
 *   A negated errno value is returned on any failure:
 *
 *   -ENOENT - There is no such work queued.
 *   -EINVAL - An invalid work queue was specified
 *   wqueue - The work queue handle
 *   work   - The work structure to queue
 *   worker - The worker callback to be invoked.  The callback will be
 *            invoked on the worker thread of execution.
 *   arg    - The argument that will be passed to the worker callback when
 *            it is invoked.
 *   delay  - Delay (in clock ticks) from the time queue until the worker
 *            is invoked. Zero means to perform the work immediately.
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   Zero on success, a negated errno on failure
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int work_queue_next_wq(FAR struct kwork_wqueue_s *wqueue,
                       FAR struct work_s *work, worker_t worker,
                       FAR void *arg, clock_t delay)
{
  irqstate_t flags;
  int ret = -EINVAL;

  if (wqueue && work && worker && delay <= WDOG_MAX_DELAY)
    {
      ret   = OK;
      flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&wqueue->lock);
      work_queue_start(wqueue, work, worker, arg, work->qtime + delay);
      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&wqueue->lock, flags);
    }

  return ret;
}

int work_queue_next(int qid, FAR struct work_s *work, worker_t worker,
                    FAR void *arg, clock_t delay)
{
  return work_queue_next_wq(work_qid2wq(qid), work, worker, arg, delay);
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: work_queue/work_queue_wq
 *
 * Description:
 *   Queue work to be performed at a later time.  All queued work will be
 *   performed on the worker thread of execution (not the caller's).
 *
 *   The work structure is allocated and must be initialized to all zero by
 *   the caller.  Otherwise, the work structure is completely managed by the
 *   work queue logic.  The caller should never modify the contents of the
 *   work queue structure directly.  If work_queue() is called before the
 *   previous work has been performed and removed from the queue, then any
 *   pending work will be canceled and lost.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   qid    - The work queue ID (must be HPWORK or LPWORK)
 *   wqueue - The work queue handle
 *   work   - The work structure to queue
 *   work   - The work structure to queue
 *   worker - The worker callback to be invoked.  The callback will be
 *            invoked on the worker thread of execution.
 *   arg    - The argument that will be passed to the worker callback when
 *            it is invoked.
 *   delay  - Delay (in clock ticks) from the time queue until the worker
 *            is invoked. Zero means to perform the work immediately.
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   Zero on success, a negated errno on failure
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int work_queue_wq(FAR struct kwork_wqueue_s *wqueue,
                  FAR struct work_s *work, worker_t worker,
                  FAR void *arg, clock_t delay)
{
  irqstate_t flags;
  clock_t expected;
  int          ret = -EINVAL;

  if (wqueue && work && worker && delay <= WDOG_MAX_DELAY)
    {
      ret      = OK;
      expected = clock_delay2abstick(delay);
      flags    = spin_lock_irqsave(&wqueue->lock);
      work_queue_start(wqueue, work, worker, arg, expected);
      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&wqueue->lock, flags);
    }

  return ret;
}

int work_queue(int qid, FAR struct work_s *work, worker_t worker,
               FAR void *arg, clock_t delay)
{
  return work_queue_wq(work_qid2wq(qid), work, worker, arg, delay);
}

证据已经明确：ESP32-S3 驱动是 `nuttx/arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/esp32s3_wlan.c`，24 个包缓冲时 `g_wlan_priv` 为 `0x3900`，32 个时为 `0x4ba0`，每增加一个缓冲约 592 字节。当前 `free=0 reserve=12` 的含义是：共享池 24 个缓冲已全部被 RX 队列、TX 队列或当前处理中的帧持有；`reserve=12` 只限制 TX 新申请，不是真正的 RX 独占池。

我还找到一个比“增加池数量”更直接的风险：RX 回调只在 `work_available()` 时排队处理。若新帧恰好在 `wlan_rxpoll()` 取空队列和退出之间到达，回调不会再次排队，RX 帧会滞留在 `rxb`，最终持续占满私有池并触发 NOBUF。最小方案是给 RX work 加受锁保护的 pending 状态，在 worker 退出前用 `work_queue_next()` 接管竞态；同时把 NOBUF 日志改成累计计数、首几次和周期性汇总，避免串口输出反过来拖慢 RX。这个改动不增加包数、不迁移 DMA/大块 payload、不改变 TCP/I2S 配置。接下来实施这个方案。

已完成 ESP32-S3 WLAN 缓冲区的最小修复，修改文件：

[esp32s3_wlan.c](/home/foam/vela/openvela/nuttx/arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/esp32s3_wlan.c:1313)

核心问题是 RX 回调与 RX work 存在竞态：

1. `wlan_rx_done()` 收包后放入 `rxb`。
2. 旧逻辑只在 `work_available()` 时排队。
3. 如果帧在 `wlan_rxpoll()` 最后一次取空队列之后到达，work 已经不可用，回调不会再次排队。
4. 帧会滞留在 `rxb`，最终占满 24 个私有 WLAN buffer，出现 `free=0` 和 NOBUF。

当前 `free=0 reserve=12` 的实际含义是：共享的 WLAN 私有池中没有空闲 buffer。`reserve=12` 只是限制 TX 申请，RX 仍然可以消耗整个池，并不是 12 个真正独占的 RX buffer。

本次修改内容：

- 增加 `rx_work_pending` 状态，避免 RX work 丢调度。
- `wlan_rxpoll()` 结束时检查 `rxb`，有竞态帧则使用 `work_queue_next()` 重新接管。
- `work_queue()` 或 `work_queue_next()` 失败时恢复状态并保留错误日志。
- NOBUF 仍然累计真实计数，但只输出前 8 次和每 64 次一次，避免串口日志拖慢 WLAN RX。
- 没有增加 `CONFIG_ESP32S3_WLAN_PKTBUF_NUM`。
- 没有迁移 PSRAM、DMA buffer 或 I2S buffer。
- 没有修改 TCP 窗口、任务优先级或 Wi-Fi 省电配置。
- 没有启用经典 ESP32 专用的 `ESP32_WIFI_WLAN_BUFFER_OPTIMIZATION`；该选项只存在于 `nuttx/arch/xtensa/src/esp32/Kconfig`，ESP32-S3 没有对应实现。

当前配置仍为：

```text
CONFIG_ESP32S3_WLAN_PKTBUF_NUM=24
CONFIG_NET_ETH_PKTSIZE=590
CONFIG_IOB_NBUFFERS=64
CONFIG_IOB_BUFSIZE=512
```

内存核对结果：

- 24 个 buffer 时，`g_wlan_priv`：`0x3900`，即 14,592 字节。
- 32 个 buffer 时，历史 map 为 `0x4ba0`，每增加一个 buffer 约增加 592 字节，8 个额外 buffer 增加约 4,736 字节，并导致 DRAM 链接溢出。
- 本次修复后仍为 `0x3900`，说明新增状态复用了原有结构对齐空间，没有增加 WLAN 私有静态池大小。
- IOB 名义容量为 `64 * 512 = 32,768` 字节，配置未改变。

# during the normal build context phase, so this wrapper bootstraps that
# phase first when needed, then applies the local backport and performs the
# real build.
# ROBOT_VOICE_TRANSPORT_HOOKS_V2: contest-local Agent source tree is authoritative.

set -euo pipefail

readonly SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
readonly OPENVELA_ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../../.." && pwd)"
readonly CONFIG_PATH="vendor/openvela/boards/contest2026_295_board/configs/nsh"
readonly HAL_PATCH_TOOL="${SCRIPT_DIR}/esp_hal_lock_backport.sh"
readonly NUTTX_BREAK_PATCH_TOOL="${SCRIPT_DIR}/nuttx_xtensa_break_backport.sh"
readonly NUTTX_RAW_EXC_PATCH_TOOL="${SCRIPT_DIR}/nuttx_xtensa_raw_exception_backport.sh"
readonly NUTTX_RAW_EXC="${NUTTX_RAW_EXC:-0}"
readonly AI_AGENT_PATCH_TOOL="${SCRIPT_DIR}/ai_agent_esp32s3_backport.sh"  # compatibility-only; never edits Agent source
readonly FFMPEG_AMIX_PATCH_TOOL="${SCRIPT_DIR}/ffmpeg_amix_backport.sh"
readonly VOICE_HOOK_HEADER="${OPENVELA_ROOT}/contest2026_295_suanliheidong/app/robot_voice/robot_voice_agent_hooks.h"
readonly MYENV_DIR="${OPENVELA_ROOT}/myenv"
readonly BUILD_SH="${OPENVELA_ROOT}/build.sh"
readonly NUTTX_DIR="${OPENVELA_ROOT}/nuttx"
readonly HAL_DIR="${NUTTX_DIR}/arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/esp-hal-3rdparty"
readonly HAL_CACHE_DIR="${OPENVELA_ROOT}/contest2026_295_suanliheidong/third_party/esp-hal-3rdparty"
readonly HAL_EXPECTED_VERSION="$(
  sed -n \
    's/^[[:space:]]*ESP_HAL_3RDPARTY_VERSION[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p' \
    "${NUTTX_DIR}/arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/Make.defs" | head -n 1
)"
readonly HAL_URL="$(
  sed -n \
    's/^[[:space:]]*ESP_HAL_3RDPARTY_URL[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p' \
    "${NUTTX_DIR}/arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/Make.defs" | head -n 1
)"
readonly -a HAL_REQUIRED_SUBMODULES=(
  components/mbedtls/mbedtls
  components/esp_phy/lib
  components/esp_wifi/lib
  components/bt/controller/lib_esp32c3_family
  components/esp_coex/lib
)
readonly AI_AGENT_OVERLAY_DIR="${OPENVELA_ROOT}/contest2026_295_suanliheidong/packages/ai_agent"

readonly VOICE_FIX_REQUIRED="${VOICE_FIX_REQUIRED:-0}"
readonly VOICE_TLS_SRC="${OPENVELA_ROOT}/packages/ai_agent/src/infra/vela_tls.c"
readonly VOICE_MIMO_SRC="${OPENVELA_ROOT}/packages/ai_agent/src/voice/mimo_voice.c"
# These are user-owned source trees.  build.sh context is allowed to prepare
# its generated context and HAL checkout, but it must not replace local source
# files before the actual make.  Override this list when the project layout
# uses different source roots.
readonly LOCAL_SOURCE_PATHS="${LOCAL_SOURCE_PATHS:-packages/ai_agent contest2026_295_suanliheidong/packages/ai_agent contest2026_295_suanliheidong/app contest2026_295_suanliheidong/board/contest_board/src}"
readonly LOCAL_SOURCE_SNAPSHOT="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/openvela-local-source-${BASHPID}"

cd "${OPENVELA_ROOT}"

snapshot_local_sources()
{
  local rel
  local archive
  local found=0

  mkdir -p "${LOCAL_SOURCE_SNAPSHOT}"
  : > "${LOCAL_SOURCE_SNAPSHOT}/paths"

  for rel in ${LOCAL_SOURCE_PATHS}; do
    if test ! -d "${OPENVELA_ROOT}/${rel}"; then
      echo "Local source snapshot: skip missing ${rel}" >&2
      continue
    fi

    archive="${LOCAL_SOURCE_SNAPSHOT}/${rel//\//__}.tar"
    # Snapshot user-owned source/config only.  Never preserve generated
    # objects/archives, otherwise restore_local_sources() can resurrect stale
    # code after a context/clean operation.
    tar -C "${OPENVELA_ROOT}" \
      --exclude=.git \
      --exclude='*.o' \
      --exclude='*.a' \
      --exclude='*.d' \
      --exclude='*.gcno' \
      --exclude='*.gcda' \
      -cpf "${archive}" "${rel}"
    printf '%s\n' "${rel}" >> "${LOCAL_SOURCE_SNAPSHOT}/paths"
    found=1
  done

  if test "${found}" != 1; then
    echo "No local source roots were found; refusing to build without source protection." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  echo "Local source snapshot created; context may not replace local source files."
}

restore_local_sources()
{
  local rel
  local archive
  local restore_root="${LOCAL_SOURCE_SNAPSHOT}/restore"

  rm -rf "${restore_root}"
  mkdir -p "${restore_root}"

  while IFS= read -r rel; do
    archive="${LOCAL_SOURCE_SNAPSHOT}/${rel//\//__}.tar"
    tar -C "${restore_root}" -xpf "${archive}"
    rsync -a --delete \
      --exclude='.git' \
      --exclude='*.o' \
      --exclude='*.a' \
      --exclude='*.d' \
      --exclude='*.gcno' \
      --exclude='*.gcda' \
      --exclude='*.pyc' \
      --exclude='__pycache__/' \
      "${restore_root}/${rel}/" "${OPENVELA_ROOT}/${rel}/"
  done < "${LOCAL_SOURCE_SNAPSHOT}/paths"

  rm -rf "${restore_root}"

  echo "Local source snapshot restored; compiling the files present before context."
}

apply_contest_ai_agent_overlay()
{
  if test ! -d "${AI_AGENT_OVERLAY_DIR}"; then
    echo "Missing contest-local ai_agent overlay: ${AI_AGENT_OVERLAY_DIR}" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  # The generated build context still resolves the package from
  # packages/ai_agent.  Synchronize the complete contest-local package there,
  # including deletions, while leaving the nested Git metadata and generated
  # build artifacts alone. restore_local_sources() restores the original
  # checkout at EXIT.
  ai_agent_overlay_applied=1
  rsync -a --delete \
    --exclude='.git' \
    --exclude='*.o' \
    --exclude='*.a' \
    --exclude='*.d' \
    --exclude='*.gcno' \
    --exclude='*.gcda' \
    --exclude='*.pyc' \
    --exclude='__pycache__/' \
    "${AI_AGENT_OVERLAY_DIR}/" "${OPENVELA_ROOT}/packages/ai_agent/"

  echo "Complete contest-local ai_agent source tree applied; build uses the contest copy."
}

cleanup_local_source_snapshot()
{
  if test -d "${LOCAL_SOURCE_SNAPSHOT}"; then
    rm -rf "${LOCAL_SOURCE_SNAPSHOT}"
  fi
}

if test ! -x "${MYENV_DIR}/bin/python"; then
  echo "Creating Python virtual environment: ${MYENV_DIR}"
  python3 -m venv "${MYENV_DIR}"
fi

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
source "${MYENV_DIR}/bin/activate"

# Keep the board-local esptool wrapper ahead of the system PATH.
export PATH="${SCRIPT_DIR}:${PATH}"

hal_tree_ready()
{
  local tree="$1"
  local submodule
  local status_line

  test -n "${HAL_EXPECTED_VERSION}" || return 1
  test -d "${tree}" || return 1
  git -C "${tree}" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
  test "$(git -C "${tree}" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)" = "${HAL_EXPECTED_VERSION}" || return 1

  # A matching top-level commit is insufficient: wireless builds require these
  # submodules to be initialized in the cached checkout as well.
  for submodule in "${HAL_REQUIRED_SUBMODULES[@]}"; do
    status_line="$(git -C "${tree}" submodule status --recursive -- "${submodule}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if ! grep -Eq '^[[:space:]][0-9a-f]{40}[[:space:]]' <<<"${status_line}"; then
      return 1
    fi
  done
}

hal_checkout_ready()
{
  hal_tree_ready "${HAL_DIR}"
}

hal_cache_ready()
{
  hal_tree_ready "${HAL_CACHE_DIR}"
}

restore_hal_from_cache()
{
  if ! hal_cache_ready; then
    return 1
  fi

  mkdir -p "$(dirname "${HAL_DIR}")"
  if test -e "${HAL_DIR}" || test -L "${HAL_DIR}"; then
    rm -rf "${HAL_DIR}"
  fi
  rsync -a --delete "${HAL_CACHE_DIR}/" "${HAL_DIR}/"

  if ! hal_checkout_ready; then
    rm -rf "${HAL_DIR}"
    echo "Local HAL cache restore failed commit or submodule validation." >&2
    return 1
    return 1
  fi

  echo "HAL restored from local cache: ${HAL_CACHE_DIR}"
  echo "HAL HEAD: $(git -C "${HAL_DIR}" rev-parse HEAD)"
}

save_hal_to_cache()
{
  local cache_parent cache_tmp

  if ! hal_checkout_ready; then
    echo "Cannot cache HAL: checkout, commit, or required submodules are invalid." >&2
    return 1
  fi

  cache_parent="$(dirname "${HAL_CACHE_DIR}")"
  cache_tmp="${HAL_CACHE_DIR}.tmp-${BASHPID}"
  mkdir -p "${cache_parent}"
  rm -rf "${cache_tmp}"
  rsync -a --delete "${HAL_DIR}/" "${cache_tmp}/"

  if ! hal_tree_ready "${cache_tmp}"; then
    rm -rf "${cache_tmp}"
    echo "Cannot cache HAL: copied checkout failed commit or submodule validation." >&2
    return 1
  fi

  if test -e "${HAL_CACHE_DIR}" || test -L "${HAL_CACHE_DIR}"; then
    rm -rf "${HAL_CACHE_DIR}"
  fi
  mv "${cache_tmp}" "${HAL_CACHE_DIR}"
  echo "HAL backup saved locally: ${HAL_CACHE_DIR}"
}

clone_hal_checkout_direct()
{
  local attempt

  test -n "${HAL_URL}" || return 1
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "${HAL_DIR}")"

  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    if test -e "${HAL_DIR}" || test -L "${HAL_DIR}"; then
      rm -rf "${HAL_DIR}"
    fi
    echo "Cloning HAL directly with Git HTTP/1.1 (attempt ${attempt}/3)..."
    if GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git -c http.version=HTTP/1.1 clone --quiet "${HAL_URL}" "${HAL_DIR}" &&
       git -C "${HAL_DIR}" checkout --quiet "${HAL_EXPECTED_VERSION}"; then
      return 0
    fi
    echo "Direct HAL clone attempt ${attempt} failed; retrying..." >&2
    if test -e "${HAL_DIR}" || test -L "${HAL_DIR}"; then
      rm -rf "${HAL_DIR}"
    fi
    sleep 2
  done

  return 1
}

reset_generated_build_state()
{
  rm -f "${NUTTX_DIR}/.config" \
        "${NUTTX_DIR}/Make.defs" \
        "${NUTTX_DIR}/staging/libarch.a" \
        "${NUTTX_DIR}/staging/libboard.a"
}

bootstrap_hal_checkout()
{
  if hal_checkout_ready; then
    if ! hal_cache_ready; then
      save_hal_to_cache
    else
      echo "HAL checkout is available and local cache is current."
    fi
    return 0
  fi

  if restore_hal_from_cache; then
    return 0
  fi

  echo "HAL checkout is missing:"
  echo "  ${HAL_DIR}"
  echo
  echo "Bootstrapping the normal NuttX build context first..."

  reset_generated_build_state

  # The stock clone helper uses the system Git HTTP defaults.  A direct
  # HTTP/1.1 clone avoids transient HTTP/2 cancellations while preserving the
  # exact revision and leaving submodule/mbedTLS preparation to NuttX below.
  if ! clone_hal_checkout_direct; then
    echo "Direct HAL clone failed; falling back to build.sh context." >&2
  fi

  # Follow openvela's normal build path so NuttX creates/clones the ESP HAL
  # checkout using the revision expected by this NuttX tree.
  if ! "${BUILD_SH}" "${CONFIG_PATH}" context; then
    echo "HAL bootstrap via build.sh context failed." >&2
    echo "Expected HAL checkout:" >&2
    echo "  ${HAL_DIR}" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  if ! hal_checkout_ready; then
    echo "build.sh context completed, but the HAL checkout was not created." >&2
    echo "Expected:" >&2
    echo "  ${HAL_DIR}" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  save_hal_to_cache

  echo "HAL checkout bootstrapped successfully."
  echo "HAL HEAD: $(git -C "${HAL_DIR}" rev-parse HEAD)"
}

refresh_demo_kconfig()
{
  local app link target
  mkdir -p "${OPENVELA_ROOT}/packages/demos"
  for app in robot_agentctl robot_voice robotctl; do
    link="${OPENVELA_ROOT}/packages/demos/contest2026_295_${app}"
    target="../../contest2026_295_suanliheidong/app/${app}"
    if test ! -e "${link}" && test ! -L "${link}"; then
      ln -s "${target}" "${link}"
    elif test ! -d "${link}" ||
         test "$(cd "${link}" && pwd -P)" != "$(cd "${OPENVELA_ROOT}/contest2026_295_suanliheidong/app/${app}" && pwd -P)"; then
      echo "Unexpected demo path: ${link}; refusing to replace it." >&2
      return 1
    fi
  done
  (
    cd "${OPENVELA_ROOT}/packages/demos"
    "${OPENVELA_ROOT}/apps/tools/mkkconfig.sh" -m Demos -o Kconfig
  )
  (
    cd "${OPENVELA_ROOT}/packages"
    "${OPENVELA_ROOT}/apps/tools/mkkconfig.sh" -o Kconfig
  )
}

prepare_build_context()
{
  reset_generated_build_state

  # The ESP32-S3 context target resets and repatches the HAL mbedTLS
  # submodule.  Run it before applying the temporary ai_agent compatibility
  # patch so the patch survives the actual compilation.
  "${BUILD_SH}" "${CONFIG_PATH}" context
}

refresh_restored_build_context()
{
  # build.sh context may prepare/copy board/application context before the
  # contest-local source snapshot is restored.  Existing source files still
  # compile after restore, but a newly-added source file can be missing from
  # the generated application source list.  Re-run the NuttX context target
  # after restore so the active contest CMakeLists.txt/Kconfig are evaluated
  # again without invoking build.sh's copy/configure phase a second time.
  echo "Refreshing build context from restored contest-local sources..."
  run_configured_make context
  echo "Restored-source build context refreshed."
}

run_configured_make()
{
  local extra_flags="-Wno-cpp -Wno-deprecated-declarations"
  local voice_hooks=0
  local cc_command
  local voice_launcher="${OPENVELA_ROOT}/contest2026_295_suanliheidong/app/robot_voice/scripts/voice_gcc.sh"
  local -a make_args=()
  if ! is_maintenance_target "$@" && grep -Eq '^CONFIG_LVX_USE_DEMO_CONTEST2026_295_ROBOT_VOICE=y$' "${NUTTX_DIR}/.config" 2>/dev/null; then
    if test ! -f "${VOICE_HOOK_HEADER}"; then
      echo "Missing contest HTTP hook header: ${VOICE_HOOK_HEADER}" >&2
      return 1
    fi
    extra_flags+=" -DROBOT_VOICE_AGENT_INTERPOSE=1"
    voice_hooks=1
  fi

  # Match build.sh's configuration environment without invoking context a
  # second time after the ai_agent patch has been applied.
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  set +e
  set +u
  source "${OPENVELA_ROOT}/build/envsetup.sh"
  set -e
  set -u
  export PATH="${OPENVELA_ROOT}/prebuilts/kconfig-frontends/bin:${PATH}"

  # Important: build only.  Do NOT run savedefconfig here and do NOT copy the
  # generated defconfig back into the board source tree.  A diagnostic build
  # must not silently mutate the persistent NSH board configuration.
  if test "${voice_hooks}" = 1; then
    # CC must contain one executable, with no wrapper-specific -- separators:
    # mkdeps parses CC -- CFLAGS -- files before invoking the compiler.
    cc_command="$(make --no-print-directory -s -C "${NUTTX_DIR}" \
      --eval='__rv_print_cc:;@printf "%s\n" "$(CC)"' __rv_print_cc)"
    if test -z "${cc_command}"; then
      echo "Unable to resolve configured C compiler" >&2
      return 1
    fi
    if ! test -x "${voice_launcher}" || ! test -f "${voice_launcher%/*}/voice_cc.py"; then
      echo "Missing executable voice compiler launcher: ${voice_launcher}" >&2
      return 1
    fi
    export ROBOT_VOICE_REAL_CC="${cc_command}"
    export ROBOT_VOICE_HOOK_HEADER="${VOICE_HOOK_HEADER}"
    make_args+=("CC=${voice_launcher}")
  fi
  make -C "${NUTTX_DIR}" EXTRAFLAGS="${extra_flags}" "${make_args[@]}" "$@"
}


is_maintenance_target()
{
  local arg

  for arg in "$@"; do
    case "${arg}" in
      clean|distclean)
        return 0
        ;;
    esac
  done

  return 1
}


run_maintenance_target()
{
  echo "Maintenance target detected: $*"
  echo "Skipping context bootstrap and all temporary HAL/NuttX/ai_agent backports."
  echo "This prevents distclean from deleting patched targets before the EXIT restore trap."

  # Source/config trees are not touched by NuttX clean/distclean.  Invoke the
  # requested make target directly and do not install the backport trap.
  run_configured_make "$@"
}


verify_voice_fix_sources()
{
  if test "${VOICE_FIX_REQUIRED}" != 1; then
    echo "Voice source policy verification: SKIPPED; contest-local ai_agent overlay is authoritative (VOICE_FIX_REQUIRED=${VOICE_FIX_REQUIRED})"
    return 0
  fi

  test -f "${VOICE_TLS_SRC}" || {
    echo "Missing voice TLS source: ${VOICE_TLS_SRC}" >&2
    exit 1
  }

  test -f "${VOICE_MIMO_SRC}" || {
    echo "Missing MiMo voice source: ${VOICE_MIMO_SRC}" >&2
    exit 1
  }

  local missing=0

  for marker in \
    'DNS start:' \
    'TCP connect start:' \
    'upload progress:'; do
    if ! grep -Fq "${marker}" "${VOICE_TLS_SRC}"; then
      echo "Voice fix marker missing from vela_tls.c: ${marker}" >&2
      missing=1
    fi
  done

  # The build wrapper must verify capability, not dictate runtime key policy.
  # Accept either lookup order as long as both the generic fallback and the
  # MiMo-specific key path still exist in get_api_key().
  local key_block
  key_block="$(
    sed -n '/static int get_api_key/,/^}/p' "${VOICE_MIMO_SRC}"
  )"

  if ! grep -Fq 'AGENT_CFG_KEY_MIMO_API_KEY' <<<"${key_block}"; then
    echo "MiMo voice key support is missing in mimo_voice.c" >&2
    missing=1
  fi

  if ! grep -Fq 'AGENT_CFG_KEY_API_KEY' <<<"${key_block}"; then
    echo "Generic API key fallback is missing in mimo_voice.c" >&2
    missing=1
  fi

  local first_key
  first_key="$(
    grep -Eo 'AGENT_CFG_KEY_(MIMO_API_KEY|API_KEY)' <<<"${key_block}" |
      head -n 1 || true
  )"

  if test "${first_key}" != "AGENT_CFG_KEY_MIMO_API_KEY"; then
    echo "Voice fix source verification: NOTE - get_api_key() checks ${first_key:-no-key} first; build allowed."
    echo "Voice fix source verification: NOTE - get_api_key() checks ${first_key:-no-key} first; build allowed."
  fi

  # The current MiMo TTS path must use incremental HTTP/Base64/WAV
  # processing and feed PCM through the voice streaming callback.  Do not
  # require the old whole-response TTS markers here: those belong to the
  # retired fixed-buffer implementation.
  for marker in \
    'TTS streaming request' \
    'mimo_tts_stream_synthesize' \
    '.stream_synthesize = mimo_tts_stream_synthesize'; do
    if ! grep -Fq "${marker}" "${VOICE_MIMO_SRC}"; then
      echo "Streaming TTS marker missing from mimo_voice.c: ${marker}" >&2
      missing=1
    fi
  done

  # Streaming TTS depends on the incremental HTTPS response path in vela_tls.
  for marker in \
    'vela_https_post_json_stream' \
    'transport stream enter:'; do
    if ! grep -Fq "${marker}" "${VOICE_TLS_SRC}"; then
      echo "Streaming HTTPS marker missing from vela_tls.c: ${marker}" >&2
      missing=1
    fi
  done

  if test "${missing}" != 0; then
    echo "Refusing to build: expected voice-chain fixes are not present." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  echo "Voice fix source verification: OK"
}

force_clean_rebuild()
{
  # ai_agent and contest sources live outside nuttx/.  Clear generated
  # external objects across the full roots.  Limiting cleanup to voice/
  # robot_voice/ leaves stale network_manager/robot_network_adapter objects
  # able to shadow the restored source.
  echo "Removing stale external ai_agent/contest build artifacts; source files are untouched..."

  find "${OPENVELA_ROOT}/packages/ai_agent/src" \
    -type f \( \
      -name '*.o' -o \
      -name '*.c.*.o' -o \
      -name '*.cc.*.o' -o \
      -name '*.cpp.*.o' -o \
      -name '*.d' \
    \) -print -delete 2>/dev/null || true

  find "${OPENVELA_ROOT}/contest2026_295_suanliheidong/app" \
    -type f \( \
      -name '*.o' -o \
      -name '*.c.*.o' -o \
      -name '*.cc.*.o' -o \
      -name '*.cpp.*.o' -o \
      -name '*.d' \
    \) -print -delete 2>/dev/null || true

  rm -f \
    "${OPENVELA_ROOT}/apps/libapps.a" \
    "${NUTTX_DIR}/staging/libapps.a"
  echo "Forcing clean rebuild so the current local ai_agent sources are compiled exactly as present..."
  make -C "${NUTTX_DIR}" clean
}


verify_built_voice_image()
{
  local elf="${NUTTX_DIR}/nuttx"

  # Skip artifact verification for maintenance targets.
  if printf '%s\n' "$@" | grep -Eq '(^|[[:space:]])(clean|distclean)([[:space:]]|$)'; then
    return 0
  fi

  if test ! -f "${elf}"; then
    echo "Post-build verification failed: missing ${elf}" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  if grep -Eq '^CONFIG_LVX_USE_DEMO_CONTEST2026_295_ROBOT_AGENTCTL=y$' \
      "${NUTTX_DIR}/.config" && \
      ! grep -aF 'robot_agentctl_main' "${elf}" >/dev/null; then
    echo "Post-build verification failed: ELF missing robot_agentctl marker" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  # The contest-local robot_voice application is independent of the
  # historical ai_agent streaming implementation.  When the legacy
  # voice_echo app is disabled, validate the new app marker and do not require
  # private symbols/strings from packages/ai_agent.
  if grep -Eq '^CONFIG_LVX_USE_DEMO_CONTEST2026_295_ROBOT_VOICE=y$' \
      "${NUTTX_DIR}/.config" && \
      ! grep -Eq '^CONFIG_LVX_USE_DEMO_CONTEST2026_295_VOICE_ECHO=y$' \
      "${NUTTX_DIR}/.config"; then
    if ! grep -aF 'robot_voice_main' "${elf}" >/dev/null; then
      echo "Post-build verification failed: ELF missing robot_voice marker" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    python3 "${OPENVELA_ROOT}/contest2026_295_suanliheidong/app/robot_voice/scripts/verify_voice_elf.py" "${elf}"
    echo "Post-build verification: contest-local robot_voice linked"
    return 0
  fi

  # The official ai_agent source does not promise the contest-local streaming
  # MiMo markers.  Only enforce them when the caller explicitly requests the
  # voice-fix source contract.
  if test "${VOICE_FIX_REQUIRED}" != 1; then
    echo "Post-build streaming voice verification: SKIPPED (VOICE_FIX_REQUIRED=${VOICE_FIX_REQUIRED})"
    return 0
  fi

  local missing=0

  # Verify that the streaming TTS implementation and streaming HTTPS
  # transport actually reached the final firmware image.
  for marker in \
    'TTS streaming request' \
    'transport stream enter:'; do
    if ! strings "${elf}" | grep -Fq "${marker}"; then
      echo "Post-build verification failed: ELF missing streaming marker: ${marker}" >&2
      missing=1
    fi
  done

  # The old fixed-buffer diagnostics should not survive in the final image.
  # Their presence usually means an old mimo_voice object/archive was linked.
  for marker in \
    'TTS response bytes=' \
    'TTS audio base64 bytes=' \
    'TTS WAV bytes=' \
    'TTS PCM output too small'; do
    if strings "${elf}" | grep -Fq "${marker}"; then
      echo "Post-build verification failed: ELF still contains legacy TTS marker: ${marker}" >&2
      missing=1
    fi
  done

  if test "${missing}" != 0; then
    echo "The firmware was built, but the streaming MiMo TTS/HTTPS sources were not linked cleanly into nuttx." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  echo "Post-build streaming voice verification: OK"
}

hal_rollback=0
nuttx_break_rollback=0
nuttx_raw_exc_rollback=0
ai_agent_rollback=0
ai_agent_overlay_applied=0
ffmpeg_amix_rollback=0
restore_backports()
{
  local rc=$?

  trap - EXIT INT TERM

  if test "${ffmpeg_amix_rollback}" = 1; then
    if ! "${FFMPEG_AMIX_PATCH_TOOL}" reverse; then
      echo "failed to restore the FFmpeg amix build backport" >&2
      if test "${rc}" -eq 0; then
        rc=1
      fi
    fi
  fi

  if test "${ai_agent_rollback}" = 1; then
    if ! "${AI_AGENT_PATCH_TOOL}" restore; then
      echo "failed to restore temporary ai_agent build compatibility files" >&2
      if test "${rc}" -eq 0; then
        rc=1
      fi
    fi
  fi

3. 为每个 buffer 建立所有权状态图。确认每个 buffer 在任一时刻恰好处于一种状态，例如 free、RX 队列、正在处理、已交给网络栈或 TX 队列；排查泄漏、重复入队、重复释放和错误归还。

# NuttX Driver Development

Follow the full driver lifecycle in order. Keep edits small and testable.

> [!TIP] This skill can be used standalone or via the `driver-workflow` agent (`agents/driver-workflow.agent.md`) for end-to-end driver development with automated reference matching, requirements generation, and PR submission.

## Preparation

### 1) Clarify scope and expectations

- Identify the NuttX driver subsystem (sensor, serial, timer, analog, etc.).
- Confirm target bus (I2C, SPI, 1-Wire, etc.) and required hardware properties.
- Clarify the NuttX source tree location. The driver code lives under `nuttx/drivers/`.

### 2) Find reference drivers

> [!NOTE] Two types of reference drivers serve different purposes
>
> - **骨架参考（NuttX API 模式）**: 优先使用 NuttX in-tree 同类驱动作为代码骨架，确保符合 NuttX 的 upper-half/lower-half 架构和 VFS 集成方式
> - **芯片参考（寄存器/时序验证）**: 优先使用 Linux/Zephyr 同芯片驱动，用于交叉验证 datasheet 的寄存器定义、初始化序列、SPI 帧格式等芯片专属知识
>
> When used standalone: 手动搜索两类参考驱动
> When used with `driver-workflow` agent: Step A.2 自动完成两条线的并行搜索

Always look at the in-tree NuttX drivers before doing any work. There might already be a driver that (best scenario at the top):

1. Is exactly the same part as the one you are working on
2. Targets a very similar part from the same vendor (e.g., BMP280 vs BME680)
3. Is the same device subsystem as yours (e.g., another I2C sensor)

If a reference driver is found, use it as a **skeleton template**:

1. Copy the source file structure (function signatures, bus access pattern, registration flow, file layout)
2. Replace all device-specific content: register definitions, chip ID values, vendor/chip names, init sequences, calibration logic
3. After generating code, grep for the original chip name — zero matches required
4. **Do NOT copy register addresses or chip-specific constants** — these must come from the target device's datasheet

Re-use these files/folders whenever possible:
- Header files in `include/nuttx/sensors/`, `include/nuttx/i2c/`, etc.
- Existing board-level registration patterns in `boards/`

If no suitable reference driver exists:

1. Use the dispatch table below to load the subsystem-specific pattern reference
2. Use the most similar subsystem's reference driver as template (e.g., use accelerometer driver as template for gyro)
3. Follow the architectural pattern (uORB vs chardev) strictly from the loaded reference
4. For 🔲 Planned subsystems, use `chardev_pattern.md` (Production-Quality Skeleton section) as the starting point

Here are the relevant folders to search for examples:

```
nuttx/
├── drivers/          # Device-specific driver sources. Search here first
│   ├── sensors/      # Sensor drivers (I2C/SPI/1-Wire)
│   ├── serial/       # UART/serial drivers
│   ├── i2c/          # I2C bus framework
│   ├── spi/          # SPI bus framework
│   ├── timers/       # Timer/watchdog/RTC drivers
│   ├── analog/       # ADC/DAC drivers
│   ├── leds/         # LED drivers
│   ├── input/        # Input device drivers
│   └── ...           # Many more subsystems
├── include/nuttx/    # Public header files for driver APIs
│   ├── sensors/      # Sensor driver headers & sensor_lowerhalf_s
│   ├── i2c/          # I2C master interface (i2c_master_s)
│   ├── spi/          # SPI interface (spi_dev_s)
│   └── fs/           # VFS file_operations, register_driver()
├── boards/           # Board-specific initialization & driver registration
└── arch/             # Architecture-specific lower-half bus implementations
```

Use `references/nuttx_nav_search.md` for driver examples and navigating the NuttX repo.

#### Pattern A: Upper-Half / Lower-Half — Preferred for Subsystem Drivers

Most NuttX driver subsystems (sensors, timers, serial, audio, etc.) use an upper-half/lower-half split. The upper-half provides the VFS interface and common logic; you only implement the lower-half callbacks.

```
Application
    │  open/read/write/ioctl/poll
    ▼
  VFS (/dev/...)
    │
    ▼
  Upper-half (provided by NuttX)  ← Generic, handles VFS + common logic
    │  subsystem-specific callbacks
    ▼
  Lower-half (your driver)  ← You implement these
    │
    ▼
  Bus API (I2C_TRANSFER / SPI_*)
```

**When to use**: Always prefer this when the subsystem provides an upper-half framework. Load the corresponding reference document from the dispatch table for implementation details.

#### Pattern B: Standalone Character Device Driver

The simplest pattern. The driver directly implements `struct file_operations` and registers with `register_driver()`.

```
Application
    │  open/read/write/ioctl/close
    ▼
  VFS (/dev/mydevN)
    │
    ▼
  file_operations  ← Your driver implements these
    │
    ▼
  Bus API (I2C_TRANSFER / SPI_LOCK+SPI_SELECT+SPI_RECVBLOCK)
```

**When to use**: Only when the device doesn't fit any existing subsystem, or when existing in-tree drivers for the same device class already use this pattern (e.g., some vibrator or custom peripheral drivers).

See `references/chardev_pattern.md` for standalone character device implementation details.

### 4) Layout the driver files

Define the files that will be created/modified. The exact layout depends on the subsystem — refer to the loaded reference document for subsystem-specific examples.

General layout:

```
nuttx/
├── drivers/<subsystem>/
│   ├── mydevice.c            # Driver implementation
│   ├── Make.defs             # Add CSRCS += mydevice.c
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Add list(APPEND SRCS mydevice.c)
│   └── Kconfig               # Add CONFIG_<SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE entry
├── include/nuttx/<subsystem>/
│   └── mydevice.h            # Public header: register function prototype
└── boards/<arch>/<chip>/<board>/src/
    └── <board>_mydevice.c    # Board-level init: get bus, call register
```

## Implementation

> [!info] TLDR
>
> - Implement C driver (lower-half callbacks OR file_operations)
> - Create public header file with register function prototype
> - Add Kconfig entry for driver enable/disable
> - Add source to Make.defs and CMakeLists.txt
> - Write board-level registration code

### Write the Driver C Implementation

For subsystem-specific implementation (sensor uORB, timer, LED, etc.), load the corresponding reference document from the Driver Type Dispatch Table above.

The following sections cover **cross-subsystem generic patterns** that apply to all driver types.

#### Bus Access (I2C / SPI)

For I2C/SPI register read/write helpers, bulk transfer patterns, SPI frame protocols (8-bit and 16-bit), and SPI mode detection — read `references/bus_access.md` when writing bus access code.

### Write the Public Header File

Create `include/nuttx/<subsystem>/mydevice.h`. The header content depends on the driver pattern:

- **Upper-half/lower-half drivers**: Header contains only the register function prototype
- **Standalone char device drivers**: Header also defines data structures for `read()`

See `references/chardev_pattern.md` for char device header examples.

### Kconfig

Add your driver entry to the appropriate `Kconfig` file (e.g., `drivers/<subsystem>/Kconfig`):

# openvela Build

编译 openvela 固件、修改内核配置、运行模拟器。

## 默认目标

默认编译目标为 goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap（64 位 ARM 模拟器）：

```
CONFIG_PATH=vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
OUTPUT_DIR=cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
```

如果用户指定了其他板级配置路径，替换上述路径即可。

## 命令

### 编译

```bash
./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake -j$(nproc)
```

示例：
```bash
./build.sh vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/ --cmake -j$(nproc)
```

**成功标志**: 输出 `#### build completed successfully`

**编译产物**: `<OUTPUT_DIR>/nuttx`（ELF）、`<OUTPUT_DIR>/vela_ap.bin`

### 修改内核配置（menuconfig）

```bash
./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake menuconfig
```

menuconfig 是交互式 TUI 界面，**不能在 AI 终端中直接运行**。提示用户在自己的终端中执行。

修改配置后保存会自动更新 `.config`。如需持久化到 defconfig：
```bash
./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake savedefconfig
```

### 运行模拟器

```bash
./emulator.sh <OUTPUT_DIR>
```

示例：
```bash
./emulator.sh cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
```

**成功标志**: 出现 `goldfish-armv8a-ap>` NSH 提示符

### 清理编译

```bash
rm -rf <OUTPUT_DIR>
```

全量清理后重新编译：
```bash
rm -rf cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/ && ./build.sh vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/ --cmake -j$(nproc)
```

## 编译流程

1. 用户指定或确认目标配置路径
2. 执行 `./build.sh <path> --cmake -j$(nproc)`
3. 检查输出最后几行是否包含 `build completed successfully`
4. 如果编译失败，分析错误日志并尝试修复（最多 3 轮）

## 编译失败处理

| 错误类型 | 特征 | 处理 |
|----------|------|------|
| 代码错误 | `error:` + 本驱动文件名 | 自动修复代码，重新编译 |
| 配置缺失 | `undefined reference` + CONFIG 相关 | 提示用户 menuconfig 开启 |
| 工具链问题 | `command not found` | 提示用户安装工具链 |
| 缓存问题 | 奇怪的链接错误 | `rm -rf <OUTPUT_DIR>` 后重编 |

## 启用新驱动的 CONFIG

如果需要临时启用某个 CONFIG 进行编译验证：

```bash
# 方法 1: 直接追加到 defconfig（推荐）
echo "CONFIG_SENSORS_BME680=y" >> <CONFIG_PATH>/defconfig

# 方法 2: 用 sed 修改 .config（临时，不持久化）
sed -i 's/# CONFIG_SENSORS_BME680 is not set/CONFIG_SENSORS_BME680=y/' <OUTPUT_DIR>/.config
```

修改后重新编译即可。

## 常用配置路径

| goldfish-arm64 (推荐) | `vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/` |
| goldfish-arm32 | `vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-armeabi-v7a-ap/` |
| 自定义板级 | `vendor/<vendor>/boards/<chip>/<board>/configs/<config>/` |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# Apply or reverse the contest-local ESP32-S3 WLAN buffer-flow backport.

set -euo pipefail

readonly SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
readonly OPENVELA_ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../../.." && pwd)"
readonly NUTTX_DIR="${OPENVELA_ROOT}/nuttx"
readonly PATCH_FILE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../patches/0026-esp32s3-wlan-buffer-flow-backport.patch"
readonly PATCHED_FILE="arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/esp32s3_wlan.c"

die()
{
  echo "ESP32-S3 WLAN backport: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

require_repository()
{
  test -f "${PATCH_FILE}" || die "patch not found: ${PATCH_FILE}"
  git -C "${NUTTX_DIR}" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
    die "NuttX checkout not found: ${NUTTX_DIR}"
}

patch_is_applied()
{
  git -C "${NUTTX_DIR}" apply --reverse --check "${PATCH_FILE}" \
    >/dev/null 2>&1
}

patch_is_ready()
{
  git -C "${NUTTX_DIR}" apply --check "${PATCH_FILE}" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

apply_patch()
{
  require_repository

  if patch_is_applied; then
    echo "ALREADY_APPLIED"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# Apply or reverse the contest-local ESP32-S3 WLAN buffer-flow backport.

set -euo pipefail

readonly SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
readonly OPENVELA_ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../../.." && pwd)"
readonly NUTTX_DIR="${OPENVELA_ROOT}/nuttx"
readonly PATCH_FILE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../patches/0026-esp32s3-wlan-buffer-flow-backport.patch"
readonly PATCHED_FILE="arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/esp32s3_wlan.c"

die()
{
  echo "ESP32-S3 WLAN backport: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

require_repository()
{
  test -f "${PATCH_FILE}" || die "patch not found: ${PATCH_FILE}"
  git -C "${NUTTX_DIR}" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
    die "NuttX checkout not found: ${NUTTX_DIR}"
}

patch_is_applied()
{
  git -C "${NUTTX_DIR}" apply --reverse --check "${PATCH_FILE}" \
    >/dev/null 2>&1
}

patch_is_ready()
{
  git -C "${NUTTX_DIR}" apply --check "${PATCH_FILE}" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

apply_patch()
{
  require_repository

  if patch_is_applied; then
    echo "ALREADY_APPLIED"
    return
  fi

  patch_is_ready || die "backport does not apply cleanly to ${PATCHED_FILE}"
  git -C "${NUTTX_DIR}" apply --whitespace=nowarn "${PATCH_FILE}"
  echo "APPLIED"
}

reverse_patch()
{
  require_repository

  if patch_is_applied; then
    git -C "${NUTTX_DIR}" apply --reverse --check "${PATCH_FILE}" ||
      die "backport cannot be reversed cleanly from ${PATCHED_FILE}"
    git -C "${NUTTX_DIR}" apply --reverse --whitespace=nowarn "${PATCH_FILE}"
    echo "REVERTED"
  elif patch_is_ready; then
    echo "NOT_APPLIED"
  else
    die "${PATCHED_FILE} is neither patch-ready nor patch-applied"
  fi
}

case "${1:-}" in
  apply)
    apply_patch
    ;;
  reverse)
    reverse_patch
    ;;
  status)
    require_repository
    if patch_is_applied; then
      echo "ALREADY_APPLIED"
    elif patch_is_ready; then
      echo "READY"
    else
      echo "UNSUPPORTED_STATE"
      exit 1
    fi
    ;;
  *)
    echo "Usage: $0 {apply|reverse|status}" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

确认 `rxb`、`txb`、`freeb` 共用同一个 `pktbuf[]` 池。`reserve=12` 不是独立的 12 个 RX 缓冲，而是 TX 分配时使用的保留阈值；RX 仍可能使用到全部 24 个缓冲。因此日志中的 `free=0 reserve=12` 表示当前共享 free pool 已耗尽。

确认的代码问题：

- RX work 调度失败时，原逻辑只留下队列中的 RX buffer，未可靠恢复唤醒，可能造成 `rxb` 永久积压。
- RX worker 的重排队必须使用当前 NuttX 版本要求的 `work_queue_next()`，并检查返回值。
- `ifdown` 原逻辑没有取消 RX/TX/retry work，也没有回收 `rxb`、`txb` 和 `dev.d_buf`，之后重新初始化队列可能使 buffer 失去所有权记录。
- 当前 NuttX 中 `work_available()` 实际检查 `work->worker == NULL`；`work_queue_next()` 必须在 work callback 中调用，且返回负 errno 表示失败。

已加入的修复：

- RX work 使用 `rx_work_pending` 和同一个 `priv->lock` 保护。
- `work_queue()` 或 `work_queue_next()` 失败时清除 pending，并通过 1 tick watchdog 重试。
- `ifdown` 取消相关 work 和 watchdog，在同一锁下回收 RX 队列、TX 队列及当前 `d_buf`。
- 增加低开销统计：
  - RX 入队/出队数量
  - RX 队列高水位
  - free pool 最低水位
  - buffer 回收数量
  - work 调度/失败数量
- NOBUF 日志继续限流，仅首 8 次和每 64 次输出汇总，不逐帧刷屏。

# openvela Build

编译 openvela 固件、修改内核配置、运行模拟器。

## 默认目标

默认编译目标为 goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap（64 位 ARM 模拟器）：

```
CONFIG_PATH=vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
OUTPUT_DIR=cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
```

如果用户指定了其他板级配置路径，替换上述路径即可。

## 命令

### 编译

```bash
./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake -j$(nproc)
```

示例：
```bash
./build.sh vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/ --cmake -j$(nproc)
```

**成功标志**: 输出 `#### build completed successfully`

**编译产物**: `<OUTPUT_DIR>/nuttx`（ELF）、`<OUTPUT_DIR>/vela_ap.bin`

### 修改内核配置（menuconfig）

```bash
./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake menuconfig
```

menuconfig 是交互式 TUI 界面，**不能在 AI 终端中直接运行**。提示用户在自己的终端中执行。

修改配置后保存会自动更新 `.config`。如需持久化到 defconfig：
```bash
./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake savedefconfig
```

### 运行模拟器

```bash
./emulator.sh <OUTPUT_DIR>
```

示例：
```bash
./emulator.sh cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
```

**成功标志**: 出现 `goldfish-armv8a-ap>` NSH 提示符

### 清理编译

```bash
rm -rf <OUTPUT_DIR>
```

全量清理后重新编译：
```bash
rm -rf cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/ && ./build.sh vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/ --cmake -j$(nproc)
```

## 编译流程

1. 用户指定或确认目标配置路径
2. 执行 `./build.sh <path> --cmake -j$(nproc)`
3. 检查输出最后几行是否包含 `build completed successfully`
4. 如果编译失败，分析错误日志并尝试修复（最多 3 轮）

## 编译失败处理

| 错误类型 | 特征 | 处理 |
|----------|------|------|
| 代码错误 | `error:` + 本驱动文件名 | 自动修复代码，重新编译 |
| 配置缺失 | `undefined reference` + CONFIG 相关 | 提示用户 menuconfig 开启 |
| 工具链问题 | `command not found` | 提示用户安装工具链 |
| 缓存问题 | 奇怪的链接错误 | `rm -rf <OUTPUT_DIR>` 后重编 |

## 启用新驱动的 CONFIG

如果需要临时启用某个 CONFIG 进行编译验证：

```bash
# 方法 1: 直接追加到 defconfig（推荐）
echo "CONFIG_SENSORS_BME680=y" >> <CONFIG_PATH>/defconfig

# 方法 2: 用 sed 修改 .config（临时，不持久化）
sed -i 's/# CONFIG_SENSORS_BME680 is not set/CONFIG_SENSORS_BME680=y/' <OUTPUT_DIR>/.config
```

修改后重新编译即可。

## 常用配置路径

| 目标 | 配置路径 |
|------|----------|
| goldfish-arm64 (推荐) | `vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/` |
| goldfish-arm32 | `vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-armeabi-v7a-ap/` |
| 自定义板级 | `vendor/<vendor>/boards/<chip>/<board>/configs/<config>/` |

"""Sync board network buffers and C++17, then run the existing board build."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
from fix_tflite_cxx_standard import configure_cxx17
from fix_link_dependencies import configure_link_dependencies, verify_active

VOICE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

BOARD_KCONFIG = {
    'CONFIG_IOB_BUFSIZE': '512',
    'CONFIG_IOB_NBUFFERS': '64',
    'CONFIG_IOB_THROTTLE': '16',
    # Bound each TCP receive queue so LLM + TTS cannot claim the whole IOB
    # pool. Increasing IOB_NBUFFERS would steal the DRAM needed by I2S DMA.
    'CONFIG_NET_RECV_BUFSIZE': '4096',
    'CONFIG_NET_TCP_DELAYED_ACK': 'n',
}

def config_values(path):
    values = {}
    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if line.startswith('CONFIG_') and '=' in line:
            name, value = line.split('=', 1)
            values[name] = value.strip('"')
        elif line.startswith('# CONFIG_') and line.endswith(' is not set'):
            values[line[2:-11]] = 'n'
    return values

def set_config_value(text, name, value):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    prefix = name + '='
    disabled = '# ' + name + ' is not set'
    replacement = disabled if value == 'n' else prefix + value
    output = []
    inserted = False
    for line in lines:
        if line.startswith(prefix) or line == disabled:
            if not inserted:
                output.append(replacement)
                inserted = True
        else:
            output.append(line)
    if not inserted:
        output.append(replacement)
    return '\n'.join(output) + '\n'

def sync_board_network_config(root):
    source = root / 'contest2026_295_suanliheidong/board/contest_board/configs/nsh/defconfig'
    target = root / 'vendor/openvela/boards/contest2026_295_board/configs/nsh/defconfig'
    if not source.is_file():
        raise RuntimeError('contest board defconfig missing: ' + str(source))
    if not target.is_file():
        raise RuntimeError('active vendor board defconfig missing: ' + str(target))

    # Update both authoritative and copied board configs. An upgrade from
    # the old 8192-byte policy must migrate instead of failing its preflight.
    for path in dict.fromkeys((source.resolve(), target.resolve())):
        original = path.read_text()
        updated = original
        for name, value in BOARD_KCONFIG.items():
            updated = set_config_value(updated, name, value)
        if updated != original:
            backup = path.with_name(path.name + '.before-robot-voice-network')
            serial = 0
            while backup.exists() and backup.read_text() != original:
                serial += 1
                backup = path.with_name(path.name + '.before-robot-voice-network.' + str(serial))
            if not backup.exists():
                backup.write_text(original)
            path.write_text(updated)
            print('[voice-build] synced bounded IOB/TCP receive settings into ' + str(path))

def verify_active_board_config(root):
    active = root / 'nuttx/.config'
    if not active.is_file():
        raise RuntimeError('board build returned success but nuttx/.config is missing')
    values = config_values(active)
    errors = [name + '=' + str(values.get(name)) + ' expected ' + value
              for name, value in BOARD_KCONFIG.items()
              if values.get(name) != value]
    if errors:
        raise RuntimeError('active NuttX configuration did not apply board audio/network settings: ' +
                           ', '.join(errors))
    print('[voice-build] active NuttX IOB/TCP receive settings verified')

def restore_legacy_backup(root):
    state = VOICE / 'scripts/.agent-adapter-state'
    manifest = json.loads((state / 'state.json').read_text())
    target = Path(manifest['target']).resolve()
    if not target.is_relative_to((root / 'packages/ai_agent').resolve()):
        raise RuntimeError('legacy backup target is outside this official Agent tree')
    if hashlib.sha256(target.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != manifest['patched_sha256']:
        raise RuntimeError('official file changed; refusing to overwrite it. Backup: ' + str(state))
    target.write_bytes((state / 'original.c').read_bytes())
